claims.text: Introducing 1–2 wt% graphene nanoplatelets into an HEA will reduce its coefficient of friction relative to an untreated HEA.
Introducing 1–2 wt% graphene nanoplatelets into an HEA will reduce its wear rate relative to an untreated HEA.
The reductions in friction and wear will persist across a wide service-temperature range.
The proposed untreated HEA has a relatively coarse matrix and exhibits conventional wear mechanisms.
Adding graphene nanoplatelets during alloy processing can produce a uniform dispersion within the HEA matrix.
Dispersed graphene nanoplatelets will form a continuous lubricating film at sliding interfaces.
Graphene nanoplatelets added to the HEA will promote in-situ grain refinement.
Graphene nanoplatelets have high intrinsic lubricity and low shear strength.
A graphene-derived low-shear-strength interfacial layer will limit direct metal-to-metal contact.
The graphene-derived interfacial layer will reduce adhesive wear.
The graphene-derived interfacial layer will reduce abrasive wear.
A refined near-surface microstructure can contribute to lower friction during sliding.
The graphene intervention will decrease frictional energy dissipation during sliding.
The intervention should remain effective from ambient temperature to elevated temperatures at which oxidation occurs.
The intervention should remain effective under high contact pressures typical of moving components.
The graphene-containing HEA may achieve a 10–20% relative reduction in friction coefficient and wear rate.
Graphene agglomeration will reduce the tribological benefits of the intervention.
Excessive oxidation or chemically reactive environments can compromise the graphene lubricating layer.

contradictions.description: The boundary conditions make uniform dispersion a prerequisite and state that agglomeration may reduce the benefit, but the falsification rule treats finding non-uniform dispersion as falsifying the efficacy hypothesis. Non-uniform dispersion would instead show that the stipulated intervention was not successfully implemented, so it would not decisively test efficacy under the stated boundary condition.
